A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPON research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-modeling, zero-shot accuracy, representation, throughput, ablation, and compression experiments in Sections 3–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Sections 3–4 and the appendices, including the scale-up, continual-pretraining, and MoE experiments.

M1.justification: The sparsification operator, input-independent activation correction, KL calibration objective, and inference-time bias folding remain unchanged. The continual-pretraining and MoE variants are also retained. Additional placement wording does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText and C4, the same language-modeling and QA tasks, and the same activation-sparsity, expert-sparsity, quantization, and pruning scenarios. The scale-up evaluation moved into the main text was already present in v2.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain TEAL, LaRoSA, WINA, R-Sparse, WAS, the network-pruning methods in Figure 3, LoRA, SCAP, and the bias-only alternatives. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, calibration settings, sparsity levels, evaluation metrics, representation-analysis sample sizes, and throughput protocol remain unchanged. v4 adds placement information to the existing scale-up discussion without establishing that those experiments used a revised configuration.

E4.justification: Both versions retain cross-dataset calibration, CKA/t-SNE analysis, bias-versus-activation learning, module/layer placement, LoRA-rank comparisons, continual-pretraining robustness, expert-budget sweeps, and quantization/pruning analyses. Reorganization introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The documented minibatch unbiased HSIC estimator used for CKA is unchanged.

E6.justification: Corresponding result tables and plots retain their values and findings. For example, Table 1 retains SPON's Llama3-8B perplexity of 7.83 at 50% sparsity, and Table 3 retains its throughput of 64.13 tokens/sec. v2 Figure 11 and v4 Figure 5 display the same scale-up results.

T1.justification: Section 2.4 and Appendices A–B retain the pruning equivalence, Fisher-weighted correction derivation, and generalization/complexity discussion. The CKA definition is also unchanged. Differences in extracted mathematical glyphs are typesetting/encoding differences, not revised mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, three principal contributions, and claimed average improvement remain substantively unchanged. The conclusion modestly softens the necessity claim: v2 says the results demonstrate that spontaneity is essential, whereas v4 says they suggest it plays a fundamental role.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly attributes the remaining performance gap mainly to fundamental information loss from using fewer parameters during sparse inference, rather than limitations of SPON. This is an added causal interpretation of retained results, not a newly tested finding. Existing transferability explanations and hardware/pretraining limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds an implementation-repository link and a down-projection-only placement statement in the scale-up discussion. These expand access information and documentation without establishing an implementation change. Training hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and Appendix D's computational accounting were already supplied in v2.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning are retained. Reference changes concern bibliographic metadata, including a revised title for Dong et al. with the same arXiv identifier, plus updates to Bick et al. and Kriegeskorte et al.; these are not new related works.

P1.justification: v4 revises the title and author/publication information, presents contributions as bullets, removes the standalone Discussion and Future Outlook section, and moves continual pretraining into Section 3.7. Section 3.3 and the conclusion receive limited rewrites, and acknowledgments are added. Most technical prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The existing scale-up chart moves from v2 Appendix F, Figure 11, to v4's main-text Figure 5. Other figures are renumbered and reflowed, and Table 10 is placed closer to its LoRA discussion. The chart designs and table contents remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves implementation discoverability, brings existing scale-up evidence into the main text, removes redundant discussion, and moderates the conclusion's necessity claim. These provide modest clarity and access gains while preserving the scientific evidence. Section 3.3's new attribution of the residual accuracy gap to fundamental information loss lacks a new supporting control, limiting the improvement.
